business_problem: EPRI needed to run advanced AI for sensitive utility documents and weather-planning workflows locally, because energy-sector research data could not leave controlled environments and shared compute delays limited how quickly researchers and planners could test new scenarios.
solution_summary: EPRI built two local AI workflows on NVIDIA deskside systems so energy researchers could keep performance, sovereignty, and compliance without relying on external networks. Power Chat runs on DGX Spark and Dell Pro Max with GB10 to host a 120B-class open-weight model, a one-million-token document cache, and inference on a single local system. It serves technical documents, logs, and reports through a natural-language interface using a NVIDIA vLLM NGC container with prefix caching, all inside air-gapped or connectivity-limited environments. For planning and grid operations, EPRI uses DGX Station with AI weather models such as GenCast, FourCastNet, CorrDiff, and CBottle to downscale weather data, generate high-resolution ensemble forecasts, and give grid planners more time to evaluate scenarios. Across both workflows, coherent unified memory, local DGX software, and on-prem deployment let EPRI prototype, fine-tune, and operate energy AI without exposing regulated data or waiting on shared infrastructure queues.

data_flow: Technical documents and logs are loaded into Power Chat’s local cache on DGX Spark for natural-language retrieval, while weather and climate grids feed DGX Station models such as GenCast, FourCastNet, CorrDiff, and CBottle to produce ensemble forecasts and downscaled outputs for grid operators and planners.
business_outcome: EPRI can now run a 120B-class local document assistant at 35 tokens per second for one user or 150 aggregate tokens per second for ten concurrent users, while DGX Station compresses a 50-member weather ensemble from an estimated 10+ CPU hours to 150 seconds, giving grid planners more time to act without sacrificing air-gapped deployment requirements.

architecture_clues: Power Chat keeps model weights, the document cache, and inference entirely on the local system and can operate air-gapped.
DGX Spark uses 128 GB of coherent unified memory to fit a 120B-class model and large KV cache on a deskside system.
DGX Station uses Grace Blackwell unified memory so EPRI can run large ensemble forecasts locally without dedicated data-center infrastructure.
evidence_quotes: Power Chat runs a 120-billion-parameter open-weight LLM entirely on one deskside system, streaming 35 tokens/second to a single researcher and 150 tokens/second aggregate across 10 concurrent users.
Both workflows run entirely on premises and are air-gap capable, with no external network dependency.
Users select technical relevant documents that are loaded into the model's memory via cache-augmented generation.
NVIDIA DGX Station GB300 generates a full 50-member GenCast ensemble weather forecasts in 150 seconds, compared to an estimated 10+ hours on a CPU server.
The result is a private, cost-effective AI assistant that keeps a one-million-token KV cache for document recall across sessions.
